info.title: Fortitude21 API: dangerous goods tools and product catalogue
info.description:
Free, keyless JSON API from Fortitude21, in two halves.

The tools answer dangerous goods packaging questions from the regulations: the UN drums, jerricans and IBCs a UN number may use and the largest size of each (ADR 2025 Table A and its packing instructions), what a UN packaging mark means, IBC test and inspection dates, the ADR 1.1.3.6 small-load points, the bund capacity a store needs under a country's rule, and jerry can quantities.

The catalogue under /api/v1/ covers what Fortitude21 makes: steel, stainless, aluminium, tinplate and UN-rated HDPE jerry cans, pails, tins, drums, spill pallets, closures and handling equipment. Search and filter by material, capacity, certification and application, fetch one product in full, compare products on the attributes they all publish, read indicative pricing, list documentation, and send a quotation request.

CORS is open and there is no key or sign-up. Every answer carries `cite` (credit it with a link) and `publisher`. The same tools are an MCP server at https://fortitude21.com/mcp.

Two things to rely on: the catalogue is read-only, with no write path at any version, and any price is indicative and never a quotation. The quotation request creates an enquiry for a person to price, not an order. Tool answers are general information; check the rules for your own load.

get.description: Type a UN number (or a substance name) and get each entry's class, packing group, limited quantity, UN mark level, and for every container type the UN codes allowed and the largest size in litres, from ADR 2025 Table A (P001, P504, IBC02, IBC03). Covers 157 UN numbers of liquids.

get.description: Totals ADR 1.1.3.6 points for a vehicle load (quantity x 50, 3 or 1 by transport category) against 1,000, or against the category maximum for a single-category load, and says whether the exemption applies and what still applies. Covers 92 UN numbers.

parameters.name: l

schema.description: Lines, comma-separated; every line is counted. Each line: UN number, packing group where the UN number has entries in more than one transport category, quantity per package (L or kg), number of packages, colon-separated. Examples: 1203:20:10 and 1263:II:20:5. A line that cannot be read stops the whole answer.

post.description: Submit a quotation request for one or more products and get a reference back. It creates an enquiry for a person to price: no price is accepted, no stock confirmed, no delivery date committed and no order created. Every part number is validated and the information still needed is named back.

413.description: The body is over 64 KB. A quotation request carries at most 20 lines and 3,000 characters of notes. Do not retry unchanged.

429.description: Rate limited. From the zone rule (about 10 requests in 10 seconds from one IP: wait 10 seconds) or the enquiry limit (10 enquiries an hour from one address, shared with the contact form: the Retry-After header gives the wait in seconds). Send each quotation request on its own: inside an MCP batch it is refused.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before sending another enquiry

500.description: The request was not accepted because of a fault on our side. Retry, or email David@fortitude21.com.

503.description: The enquiry store could not save the request, so it was not accepted. retry is true: try again later, or email David@fortitude21.com.
